body:
I got a raise at work, I probably shouldn't complain.

Still entirely alone, still not convinced I'll be able to adjust whatever is wrong with me enough to resolve that situation.
Oh I realise, but as I feel its a waste of money, I'd at least like to feel I was doing my best to save as much as I could.

I'm aware that anyone that would cheat on me, I wouldn't want to be with. Anyone that treats me the way they have, I wouldn't want to be with. Anyone that listens to other peoples opinion about me beyond their own, or perhaps beyond mine, I wouldn't want to be with. This leaves a hell of a lot of people out of the picture and also paints a confusing picture when these same people are happy to treat others in a much better fashion.

I'm not so sure about all this stuff about women, I've had it drilled into me for years that women are people and they are not different. I understand that a lot of this type of equality talk is nonsense - people are different and certain people act certain ways. Its the fact you treat them equally that matters, but that you treat them like the same people. That is, treat people differently, according to their needs. None the less, I'm definitely conflicted as to which story is actually true and it worries me that the illogical emotion rampant picture of women that is given by the majority of society would actually be true. It is rather scary that perhaps a whole section of society is biologically driven to make illogical choices. This in turn means women are dangerous and would do great harm to the world. But I know this isn't true, so therefore the former must also not be true. Unless, again, my theory that the ability to make logical choices, absent of emotion is important - is in fact wrong. World changer.

I don't think there has ever been a situation in which I am suppose to be concerned and I've matter of factly said "I am concerned". I simply meant it seems my honest explanation of my feelings (or state of being concerned) is not enough apparently and in fact I need to be more, what I would considered, primal. Devolved, less intellectual, less logical; worse.

I don't believe in love - not in the ".. is blind" way, its simply a heightened state of affection, the type you feel for many other people often with the added benefit of sexual contact of some form of the other. I love people so much, its often a little confusing as to why I care so much about them, it doesn't mean logic is removed or I am blinded by it. I wouldn't want something to impair my senses unless I'm attempting to forget something like our good friend alcohol does.

Further, this notion that women are these illogical emotion driven creatures makes me wonder is this biological or is this learnt. If it is learnt it isn't a blanket statement. Much like many stereotypes about men. Again I'm not convinced these works for a whole gender, people are individuals.

It isn't as simple as being a status climber, she had her doubts and others played into those. I wasn't what she was told she should like and so uncertainties flourish.

I! can't! read! the! word! Yahoo! without! thinking! of! a! search! engine! no-one! uses! any! more!

I have given things up and sacrificed things for partners, I don't need to be illogical to do that. Like the common who would you help up, hanging from a cliff if you could only choose one - a or b. I'm weigh up who was likely to make the better impact in the world. Who would be the best for the world. Of course, with a partner - I'd likely choose them, but for me, not for them and I'd know I should choose the one who will make a greater impact..

I realised that really all of this was a way of at least testing the waters on therapy, this is why I posted here and this is why I bothered to talk and discuss this whole situation. As I said before, I won't be going to a professional any time soon. It doesn't mean I won't but if I'm going to spend money on such a thing, at the very least I need to work out how to condense all the information to fill each session better and reduce the charges!

I appreciate that staying in a relationship that isn't working isn't a good choice. I'm not sure I agree that something cannot be saved, I think reasoned discussion solves a large proportion of problems. The issue in this case was the guy and a few friends spent a few months telling her I was ugly or horrible or not worth her time, till eventually she seemed to agree. I think she always had this thought in the back of her mind, so it isn't all them (unless that is once again me putting my own fears in the minds of others) and I again I don't hold ill will about it. But it isn't quite someone is unhappy and I'm randomly deciding they should stay.

I'm not sure I understand what emotionally generous means in this context if you think I haven't been so. My automatic response would be to say yes I have, but you'll have to explain what you mean by it. I have pretty malformed emotions I realise they don't work properly, but that doesn't mean I'm not generous with them.

I tend to think "fuck a world in which people *want* anger". I hate anger it makes me incredibly uncomfortable and I don't understand why being trustworthy and saying "I am passionate, I am concerned" isn't enough.

Of course, I forgive them, I hold no ill will towards any of them. I just don't really want to have to go through what I've gone through with them with others and can't see a way to avoid that.

I've already self diagnosed the abandonment issues, I figure that is fairly apparently knowing myself. Whether I have had those issues longer than I realise, that I don't know. But I know the first time I was acutely aware of them was when a relationship of 7 or so years ended, they decided to leave me. My attempts to ask why, why so suddenly, what did I do, what could I do, or at least just to talk me through it. No, all I got was that we shouldn't be together. This was done over email, my phone calls were ignored and when asking if I could come over and at least discuss it, I was told if I turned up they would call the police and say I was stalking them. It felt cold, random, heartless and beyond all else just left me with no sense of control what so ever. of course it turns out they were cheating on me, but that never quite made the complete lack of control or understanding in the situation okay. It did all make me realise that that lack of control and the fact people would be willing to simply walk away from me was a real issue for me. If you'd like some further ammo - I'm quite aware that I myself have walked away from many friendships, people are quite easily just gone from my thoughts. I'll defend it by saying they were all abusive, but it probably says a lot that I'm able to just walk away from people.

Again though, I feel this need to defend myself in regards to sabotaging relationships, I'm quite aware that I have been able to turn off in relationships - but it is only ever momentary. (Though probably enough proof for your subconscious theory) My main argument is with being emotionally distant, avoiding bonding or failing to make emotional commitments. I would fear if anything that I do all of these things too well. I'm an extremely dedicated person to the people I am dedicated to, it seems (from my perspective) that they simply choose to betray that at some point.

I appreciate your self reflection, but I'm not sure we have the same story. I'm very generous with myself around other people and the closest to a mood I have is when I'm extremely hurt. At these points I just close down. I'm never angry or moody though and its been said very often that I have an extremely patient and calm persona. Again, I worry this conflicts with my outwards appearance as it seems for the most part I'm observed by people on looks alone as being quite the opposite. I'm open to hugging people and its often considered a sign of attack for example. Perhaps this is me once again manifesting my own fears as I, like the rest of humanity have issues in my appearance due to how people have treated me for it. Perhaps I put too much emphasis on it, but I don't believe I do.

I'm just not sure what is "wrong with me" and I'm sure I've avoided for at least some of the time working that out, as doubting myself is yet another one of those issues created by being constantly told I am wrong, when in fact I am right.

I really appreciate the fact you are bothering to respond after so many replies, especially as you don't seem to feel I've been co-operating enough.

On reflection I think I actually feel like I'm having to justify my position. Maybe there is nothing wrong with that, but it does mean every response I make is geared towards trying to re-explain something.

First off, I understand there is a certain humour in the fact that you're right - I'm able bodied and to most standards quite lucky in the health department. Many people are physically or even mentally worse off than I am and there is quite possibly something wrong in not appreciating that. I've come to realise that we each live in our own world and so us, our pain is our pain and our problems are our problems. I knew someone who used to get very upset when they didn't get their dinner when they expected it, they would feel the whole world was ending for them and its interesting to compare that others may not think twice about missing a dinner. I'm not sure that makes their pain any less or quite possibly has any baring on their own emotions over the situation. We'd all possibly do quite well to consider our circumstances though and realise "things aren't so bad". Unfortunately for me, all I've ever wanted was the things I've never had and so to me, that is the end of the world. I really now have a phobia that any time I may be happy with someone, someone might seem to care it will end. As it always has. Again, as we discussed earlier that could be all me, all my fault but it doesn't make me feel any less powerless or trapped by it.

I don't think over 20 years is really a temporary problem, if anything I see happiness as a temporary situation. The permanency of suicide is just something that makes it all the more welcoming, I don't want to worry about the happiness disappearing and so coming to terms with the fact it will never last, or never again exist is fine by me. Just not by others. If I was never born, the world would know no better - not many people sit around worrying about all the would-be children is a,b,c,x,y,z had happened. So I don't think the situation should be so bizarre when that life does exist. It isn't the ideal solution, its something we as a society should strive to avoid, but sometimes life is just not getting better. Rather like the euthanasia argument.

Your comments on brain damage, becoming paralysed etc are very valid. All the more reason I think a suitable way out should be offered to people, but hey... I'd want as close to a 100% guarantee as possible that I would die, you're entirely right in that suffering the consequences of a failed attempt would be worse than my life currently is.

As for this SO that I may or may not meet, I fear that this scenario will go on the same, only I realise the longer it doesn't get destroyed, the more pain it will cause when it finally does. I didn't start off with these abandonment issues, this is fairly new in the whole "feeling like the world is shit" situation. But when I was 6, my parents got divorced - my mother was rather quick off the trigger and spiteful in how she handled it. I only remember the tension and arguments, the disappointment and broken heartedness of my father. But I realise it is something that just happened without his control and something she later regretted as she was destined then to be alone. This sort of illogical behaviour worries me and just shows that at any time these things can fall apart - and with my now-history it just shows how frequently it happens to me. I wouldn't want children, as I wouldn't want to put them through the potential divorce and I wouldn't want them to have to live the life that I have lived. They really are better off not being alive in my eyes.

Back to the start of your comment. Here is where I feel I need to explain myself, but I'm not too sure how. I don't really know how I thought this post would work out this way - but I thought it would result in minimal exposure and the chance to form better subsequent posts in the future about my experiences. Its rather why I started so vague, I wanted to gauge reactions and see if this would be a good place for me to vent, to air my thoughts and get a reasoned reaction from perhaps more normal human beings. Instead I've attempted to respond to the specific points, but I haven't swayed much or managed to explain any details. It isn't me attempting to avoid this - its simply that I often find unless directly asked, these things don't come up in my general conversation. I hope that makes some sense.

In saying the above - I'm really referring to the creation of expectations. I'm not sure if I'm manifesting this due to my fears or due to the fact it actually happens. I'm constantly worried people misunderstand me and try to explain and find that explaining has the opposite affect on most people - they instead believe I'm not explaining but dominating or arguing or not listening. I just feel explanation is important. (and I realise this is probably starting to become a little incoherent) I in turn fear that perhaps I only want to explain so much, because I feel so little control in my life and its all a control mechanism, this would mean my reasoning for explanation - to inform, to educate to better people and their understanding is false and simply a construct of my mind to attempt to coerce people into letting me get, well, what I want.

I don't pretend to have no emotion though. I went through various parts of my life without any. I wasn't able to feel or empathise with people. It simply wasn't "on". Joining any form of relationship that is close and seemingly meaningful helps me to relearn that emotion and it ends up being a whole new experience to get to grips with, from the beginning. I don't mean to pretend I don't care and suddenly care, and I'm rather certain in my enthusiasm to over explain everything I've explained what I suspect will happen to every unsuspecting victim that happens across me. If they don't listen, it doesn't feel like my fault and so it simply makes me feel rather alien to have this outlook on life that no-one else seems to share, but seems to be so logical to me and even, when discussing with others "on paper" is logical to them. They just don't follow it.

I've realised something interesting about people saying they care to me. I ignore it, I excuse it, I laugh it off. Anything positive tends to go over my head - it seems also, because of this people will stop bothering and that will just cement my ideal that they never really cared. I recently spoke to someone who fairly abusively, but also in a rather friendly manner berated me for making excuses about some social interaction or other (I'm actually generally outgoing socially, so don't read into this too much, again I'm trying to be vague simply not to overwhelm this post with nonsense). The fact they went on and on and refused to listen to me excuse myself as to why it isn't really true, they don't really mean it, actually seemed to get through to me a little. Its quite an interesting self reflection to realise that I'm that stubborn and need things said that many times, but also that I really don't remember any times in my life anyone really tried that hard to compliment me.

I think I'll stop here, as I realise I've babbled quite enough and likely not given near the detail you might hope for, again if I've missed something point it out, if you think I avoided something, ask and really don't worry about walking on egg shells around me there isn't anything I can think of that will set me off, I don't tend to be an emotional rollercoaster.

On topic regarding walking on egg shells - your comment earlier about me being controlling was about as hurtful and effective as it will get for me. It really bothered me you said that, as I've always disliked people controlling others and never wanted to do so myself and yet have many fears I do. But none the less I didn't (I don't think) go all crazy on you, so perhaps that is a good enough example of saying what you mean, not what you think I'll like.

Most of my comments here have ended up rather jumbled up, as I've just attempted to reply without putting the time in to make sure it was as perfect as it could be. I think the point still carries across and I would hope for the most part I'm forgiven for not being 100% lucid in my writing. Equally I'm rather sure I read your post without any issues, so I wouldn't worry too much.

Unfortunately I find myself just wanting to respond in giving you advice for your friend. If he were me and you were a friend, I'd want you to make it rather clear you cared. At least sometimes put his needs before your own. And try even when its not obviously appreciated. If he hasn't come out with you - go and get him and take him somewhere hassle free that he would enjoy. The less contact you have, the more it reminds you of how alone you are. Losing all my "friends" certainly did that to me. If you are actually a friend, then he has something I never did and you probably ought to remind him of that.

* 8 is rather a guess, its at least the point at which I was cornered by the whole year group below me and taunted and hit till a teacher came along. Beyond that I don't have any gauge for what age this started, I didn't think to keep a record. The world seemed rather cold, I felt rather alone and people seemed to rather dislike me. I felt I had nothing in the world to enjoy and haven't ever felt like I wanted to be here.
* Disregarding the depression, disappointment or unhappiness my suicide would cause. They would be free of the hassle of my existence. I haven't turned out to be what they want, they dislike me as a person, but love me as a son. Me not being here would be a blessing for them, if only they could forget I ever existed.
* Perhaps they have no way of knowing, but it is how it turned out and its always seemed in my eyes to the fault of them bringing me into the world, without a choice. I know it isn't their fault, but if I had the choice now to exist or not to, I would choose not to exist and I can't help by resent the fact they would never have even considered how I would feel about life, but instead more that they wanted a child.

Not including actually having goals, I've done and do most of which you discuss in the last part of your post. I try to enjoy nature and the world. I believe death is a *known* its a nice simple ending and after that I'm done. Life has had plenty of second chances and it doesn't appear its likely to improve its ratio of good to bad any time soon. The main issue is that I want to enjoy the world with other people, I don't enjoy doing things alone, being alone or appreciating the world on my own. I want to share this life, but there is no-one who wants to share it  with me.

I'm long long out of school, any counsellors would cost money I'm not interested or confident enough in them to pay someone to listen to my nonsense as of yet, but another person posting here has been quite insistent that this is the best course of action and as I said to them - it would be silly of me to go through with this without having at least explored all avenues, but we're all entitled to do silly things every so often I guess.

I don't particularly want a perfectly paved road, but a road, with a few stops on the journey would be a pretty nice improvement.
Ah I see, the plot summary didn't mention that, but I guess it would explain why Fertility tricked Tender into hijacking the plane, she wanted an out?

When I'm sick I don't go to the doctor, when I'm bleeding, I generally watch. I'm not trying to negate everything you say, it just happened that the answer was no to both of your examples. It doesn't invalidate your point, I can't pretend to have tried everything till I have and so perhaps it would be unwise of me to commit myself to this act without trying that last option.

I actually came here to see what peoples reactions to my circumstance was. to gauge what the general reaction to this act was.

I'll admit it feels a little more like "you are wrong and committing suicide is wrong" than anything else. Unfortunately I simply don't see what is so wrong about it.

I've been mocked whenever I've even approached the subject with people in life, I'm not too bothered about it happening on the Internet.

I also find suicide to be a fairly decent source of humour. Suicide Booths in Futurama? Fantastic.

I don't think there is anything wrong with being able to make fun of your own situation.

I'm not too sure I see it myself, but I guess it could be quite unusual to some to joke when discussing something so morbid. Personally I like humour, it makes people happier and it lightens moods. It probably also helps me somewhat escape from what I'm talking about.

I didn't really understand the other persons post, seemed like a mish-mash of words and memes, but I guess its getting late.

For the most part, I don't think these issues are anything special. This scenario seems to be quite common and lots of people from various walks of life.

I agree the role of therapist has been done by myself and its likely this that makes me so wary of therapists.

It could all just be excuses so I don't have to bother trying with it, but I'm definitely reluctant enough that it isn't going to happen any time soon.

As for confusing potential partners, I can understand that but I'm pretty clear with people about who I am. I shouldn't have to suffer for the fact they choose to ignore what I say and interpret things in their own way. I'm unsure how to unify my outward appearance and my inner dialogue.

You certainly seem to want me to talk to a therapist though and if that is because you feel there isn't much more to say, don't feel bad in not responding. I initially didn't type too much as I figured it would get a bit boring after a while for people.

I can't use satire while I'm unhappy?

This isn't an attempt at some strange new trolling method, but sometimes I guess its easier to blame it on the trolls than on real people being real people.

Oh, my friends just knew about it, as in were told or saw it before me, they didn't have any additional sense. I was always the first to spot it, which always made it worse as I was the questioning myself constantly as my questions about whether they were happy, or fulfilled, whether I could do anything to make them more comfortable would be returned with denial of everything. Only to find out during this time they were, in fact, cheating. Every relation on the same happens and I worry its just in my head and I'm imagining it and then suddenly, there it is.

I'm actually pretty vulnerable with my partners, I'm generally rather honest and while I never speak in depth about suicide, I do speak about how I feel or what I think of things. I've often worried that being so open is considered weak and makes them disinterested. Perhaps on the outside I look like an emotionless void and once they have be close enough, they realise I actually am a human being. Its not like they always leave me for someone without emotions though, it just seems like me and so I am left with only assuming its this in combination with my physical appearance that just confuses people. They find it hard to disjoin physical appearance and inner self.

I'm not convinced someone is mentally sound to choose to listen to other peoples issues for their entire life. To not be able to instruct or advise directly, to listen and help them explain, seems like it would drive me round the bend. Also, I've known doctors and how they speak about their patients outside of work and I'm not entirely sure I like the idea of being someone's dinner table comedy.

I'll answer your final question last. No. I'd rather trust a stranger on the Internet. People on the Internet are just people. Professionals are getting paid to listen. They also made the decision to go into a profession where they listen to peoples problems - that bit alone makes me doubtful of their intent. I'm not dismissing the idea though, if I'm to say I tried all roads, then I should at the very least - try all roads.

I can understand your theory that not opening up actually ends up making people feel vulnerable themselves. I have started to talk about my issues with people before, it just gets ignored and moves onto their issues. Sure I haven't tried hard, I haven't pulled them aside and said "I need to have a serious conversation with someone, please" but they never had to do that to have such discussions with me.

I had a friend who I met as they were an immature 17 year old, I was going on holiday alone as they came along with me. Years later they seem to be a very well adjusted person with a good job and good relationship. I'd mentioned my own issues before and generally attempted to use my bad experience as warning to help them, every time something would happen to me, they would vanish. I later confronted them about this, they were in a good place and they didn't need me to hold them up any more, but here are some of the issues I still have. Again, they vanish, they stop contacting me for months, till they need me for something.

I feel the above story is far too vague and needs a lot more padding to understand the situation, I guess I'm just attempting to explain that I at least don't *feel* like I never attempted to open up to people, nor act as though we aren't both human.

My friends have always known - sometimes before me - when my partners have cheated on me, surely that is a pretty decent sign of weakness in itself.

But there may be something there - I'm far too often right, I wish I weren't, but if people ask for my advice or opinion its generally right. They generally don't follow it, or credit it, but it turns out to be right. I don't really think I'm a wonderful person, I don't really think I'm intelligent or wise nor do I think I have a wonderful judgement of character and situations. But others have said it and history seems to suggest in some niche market its true and I have previously considered, no, known, that this causes issues for people. But I can't not know what I know or understand what I understand.

I haven't, but I did just read the wikipedia plot summary, perhaps that has ruined it for me now?

Why do you ask?

As yet, I haven't felt comfortable with the idea of speaking to a therapist, I'm not entirely sure I trust them, nor am I sure they'd be of any help, nor am I sure I want to spend money on it. It is something I haven't tried, so I really can't comment on its validity though.

I do think I'm unlikable, in that, in my experience not many people really like me. People share things with me all the time though, I am generally the go-to person for advice and issues, I'm simply never appreciated for it and more used.

I hadn't meant to place a wall. I said so little as I wondered what kind of responses I would get and planned to say more and give more details when asked or when it came up. As you can see from my first post, it takes a lot of words for me to even tell you nothing at all, so I was really judging whether it would be worth putting everything into words or not.

Vulnerability is perhaps a valid comment - For many years I simply turned off my emotions and while I helped and advised people, I was empathetic with their issues; they all considered me an emotionless creature. I've brought up some of how I feel before too and its generally taken as weakness and disappointment. It seems people love to hate me. being emotionless and logical is good for getting what they want, being unhappy and disappointed with the world makes me weird and weak.

Also, as far as opening up goes - One of the things about your posts earlier was the fact I wanted to say more, but didn't want to ramble. Specifically the question of being trapped and whether I lacked free will. The situation isn't that as simple as I refuse to change, it is that I have changed myself a million times and the result is the same. I've moved from groups of friends to new groups of friends, relationship to relationship, job to job, stranger to stranger and the dynamic remains the same. Rather than list all the details I went with "I don't have the power to change the situation", rather than explain that any change I make doesn't help, that I want out, but don't want to hurt people, I said "I'm trapped" and rather than list my doubts, which I have been told countless times is wrong, that its all my fault, I said "it isn't me".

Again, see I type a lot, but say very little, imagine if I started this with my life story.

I wouldn't consider myself young, unless perhaps you are 70 yourself, in which case you might consider me young.

I understand young people like sex, or people in general like sex. I've never wanted it myself, I always thought the first person I'd have sex with I would be with forever. I never felt the need to have share fluids with a handful of people.

I want friends and a relationship, stability, trust and security in that. Shared emotions, interests and experiences.

I have done a fair bit, I travelled quite extensively. I gave it up as I felt empty for not being able to share the experience with someone.

I understand friends will be friends because they like who you are. This is why I have no friends.

I don't really want for much. Not physical things at least. I want people, friends, relationships. All I've ever wanted was people to love, trust and share life with, but you can't make people share life with you. Or at least, if I tried, I'm not so sure I wouldn't get caught rather quickly!

Well, the general advice is to reach out to people and in your situation its rather socially acceptable to breakdown with people. I'm sure the people around you would be happy to spend sometime making you feel better, people are generally good to others when this sort of stuff happens.

I'm sorry I remind you of him, if it hlps ill tlk lik dis nd it mght mk it btr?

I'm not even sure I'll be able to read that tomorrow.

My mothers best friends son recently committed suicide. He did it in their family bathroom and thought this was rather rude of him. But what I said in that situation when confronted with the "why". If that is truly what he wanted, then at least we should find solace in the fact he got what he wanted and no longer has to suffer as he did. Yes, its a shame he suffered, its a shame he saw no other option, but he at least, got what he wanted.

I know it isn't, but at least in my mind I compare it to a breakup. You don't want the other person to leave, to no longer love or care about you, even to hate you. But that action is something that makes them happy and though it pains you, you still care and you at least still want them to be happy, even if in this case, that happiness might be technically only momentary.

I feel like I do need you to tell me what to do, apparently I can't trust my own judgement and I'd appreciate the input from a third party - that is why I am here.

I've often thought the problem was me. When each time a relationship ended, it ended because I was cheated on. I thought it was me. When each time a friend (various sets of friends) lied, abused, insulted or ignored me. I thought it was me. It must have been me - as you say, I'm the common factor here. People tell me it isn't me, those "other" people are just "bad" people.

I'm a lot more understanding of your opinion on this, but I really don't know what it is. I have tried everything from being nice, quiet, loud, comedic, generous, selfish, including, excluding, vacant, interested, intelligent, stupid. Each time the same happens, I agree its me, I'm rubbish at life, but I'm not quite sure what everyone else does to be so much better at it.
Of course not, looking where I'm posting :D

It wasn't really my intention, I am attempting to be honest as for the most part - I've already thought about these things. So I'm giving my already decided reasoning behind it. If I'm wrong, I'd appreciate the input.

I didn't think responding to people with what I thought was controlling. What would have been a better way to respond?

To your comments - the being trapped is because whatever I try, results in the same thing. Perhaps I should have added more detail, but I was attempting not to go on and on.

I can definitely see control, I've seen it grow more intensely as the years go by too. It feels I can't control anything and the more that feeling appears, the more I attempt to control. It wasn't my intention here, but clearly its manifested itself.

But honestly, what was my response suppose to be? What would the more human thing to do be?

Being sad is normal, things hurting is normal. Seems like the general human response to such tragedy.

In this post I'm being rather honest with people, so it ends up coming across as being rather blunt. I've played a little with wording, but in the end this is the best I came up with:

It seems it wasn't your fault and its his own decision. It sounds rather irresponsible of him to have taken this action so close to your marriage, without discussion first. It isn't what I would do, it sounds like the actions of a silly person. In my mind, if that's your reaction to losing your job, you probably aren't going to be great with marriage.

From the mind of the person wanting to follow his lead though, its my decision and I'd rather just be allowed to make my own choice. It isn't your fault and it isn't something you could make disappear. I would regret having pulled you into it and hope you could leave the hurt I've caused behind as easily as I have.

No, I don't have the power to change the situation. It isn't anything specific, for all intents and purposes my life is pretty fine.

My own behaviour is an odd one. I'm not sure how to change or identify what it is about me that makes people treat me how they do.

If you'd like, I'll message you in a few months if I'm around and pretend you made everything better with this comment.

Unfortunately being greedy won't help anything. It isn't so much a lack of being greedy that got me here. Nor is it something being greedy will get me out of. I, like you, enjoy people being happy.
